latin.607: §. XXII. Interim annotandum operæ pretium ducimus, Reformatos realissimam corporis & sanguinis Christi in S. Cœna præsentiam, Spirituali scil. modo factam, ad unum omnes seriò totôque pectore credentes ac profitentes, Spiritualem tamen præsentiam hanc, ad exemplum Veterum Ecclesiæ Doctorum, non uno eodemque simpliciter, sed sub levi quodam discrimine, Modô admodùm duplici, exponere consuevisse, ita quidem, ut alii hîc SPIRITUALITATEM in ipso Christi corpore & sanguine, in Cœna omnino præsentibus; alii in præsentiæ horum modo potiùs, quæsiverint locaverintve.
latin.608: Dico ad exemplum Veterum Ecclesiæ Doctorum: Nam PRIORI Expositioni inhærentes Patres ita inducit Joh. Jonston, Syntagmate de Communione Vet. Ecclesiæ cap. 3. Art. 2. §. 3. p. m. 75. & 76.: Multas apud Patres appellationes & epitheta, Corpus hoc Eucharisticum sortitur: Augustino dicitur Virtus & gratia; Ambrosio, Corpus divini Spiritus, quia Spiritus est; Corpus Dei, quod Corpus spirituale est; Hieronymo Caro spiritualis; intelligibilis, Isychio; Corpus typicum & symbolicum, Origeni… Bertramus vocat Corpus Spirituale; Corpus quod mysterium Dei dicitur, non visibile, nec palpabile; diversum à corpore quod in Christi corpore per resurrectionem jam glorificatum cognoscitur…
latin.609: POSTERIORI verò Expositioni ex Veteris Ecclesiæ Patribus propius accedunt à Guilielmo Forbesio allegati… PRIORI Expositioni ex Reformatis pauciores adstipulantur; Ex Neotericis Anglis vide fis Simonem Patrick, in Mensa mystica… Ex Germanis, Virum Clariss. Johann. Georg Wachterum… Horum uterque SPIRITUALITATEM corporis Christi in S. Cœna adeò urget, ut in locum corporis Christi, Spiritum ejus expressè substituere deprehendatur. POSTERIOREM expositionem plerique sequuntur.
latin.610: A munere nostro Theologico haud alienum videri potest, Ecclesiæ nostræ Marchicæ Symbolicam Confessionem Toruniensem de Cœna Domini… adduxisse in medium, quâ nullam de Cœna vidimus excellentiorem plenioremque: Constat igitur, inquiunt Torunienses, hoc Sacramentum rebus terrenis, pane & vino, & cælestibus, corpore & sanguine Domini, quæ diverso quidem modo, utraque tamen verissimè, realissimè, ac præsentissimè nobis exhibentur; nempe, Terrena, modo naturali, corporali & terreno; Cælestes verò MODO SPIRITUALI, MYSTICO ET CŒLESTI, quem Rationi & sensui inscrutabilem sola Fide tenemus… Hinc etiam Res terrena, Panis & Vinum, verè sunt & dicuntur ipsum corpus & sanguis Christi, nonquidem Substantialiter, aut CORPORALITER, sed SACRAMENTALITER & MYSTICE, seu, per & propter unionem Sacramentalem, quæ non consistit in nuda Significatione, neque tantùm in Obsignatione, sed etiam in CONJUNCTA ILLA ET SIMULTANEA REI TERRENE ET CŒLESTIS, quamvis diversimoda, EXHIBITIONE ET COMMUNICATIONE.
latin.611: POSTERIOREM hanc expositionem & ego potiorem arbitror, addens: Idem corpus Christi, quod pro nobis crucifixum est, & sanguinem eundem, qui pro nobis effusus est, in Cœna SPIRITUALITER præsentia esse & à nobis SPIRITUALITER accipi, imò etiam, quatenus tùm istud crucifixum, tum hic in ara crucis effusus est… tam verbis Institutionis Christi… quàm naturæ rei, propius accedit… Unde porrò… ingeniosè sic colligente Illustrissimo Principe Lutheranô, Philippo Hassiæ Landgravió, in Epistola ad Lutherum pro Zwinglianis…: Cumque Christus, scribit, quia clarifactum corpus habet, quo Venter cibari nequit, vix aliter manducari possit, quàm à Credentibus & per fidem; Hæc, inquam, cum ita se habeant, mihi sententia vestra videtur durior & non necessaria esse.
latin.612: §. XXIII. Itaque Reformatorum constans animi sententia est, verum & substantiale corpus Christi, quod olim in terris fuit exinanitum, nunc verò in cœlis exaltatum, sub ea qualitate, eóque modô, Communicantibus modernis semper & usquedum Christus rediturus est ad judicandum vivos & mortuos, in Cœna S. adesse, sub qua qualitate quóve modô primis Communicantibus, in ipso Sacro Cœnæ usu, præsens fuit: Neque enim minùs Reformatorum Fidei obvium est, corpus Christi crucifixum, quatenus crucifixum est, (SPIRITUALITER scil.) in Cœna præsens esse, quàm Lutheranæ Fidei adhuc persuasum manet, glorificatum corpus Christi, eóque Spirituale, quatenus tale, ore tamen corporis, manducari. Disputanti autem atque arguenti: vel, re ipsa præsens esse, & Spiritualiter adesse, pugnare inter se; vel, spiritualem adessendi modum, in corpus non competere, non possumus non recitare, quæ admodùm acutè Catechesi Racoviensi, simili pactô inferenti, Mattheus Wren Anglus respondet… AD PRIUS quidem: Ain verò Tu, inquit, re ipsa, atque spiritualiter, pugnare? tam infensa est spiritualis conditio, ut Realem devoret?… Etenim, quò magis spirituale quid est, eò magis esse id, dignosci potest…

pass_a.607: §. XXII. Meanwhile we judge it worth the labor to note that the Reformed, all to a man seriously and with whole breast believing and professing the most real presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Sacred Supper — made namely in a Spiritual mode — have yet been accustomed to expound this Spiritual presence, after the example of the Old Doctors of the Church, not simply in one and the same way, but under a certain light difference, in a Mode quite double — so indeed that some have sought and placed SPIRITUALITY here in Christ’s body and blood themselves, altogether present in the Supper; others rather in the mode of their presence.
pass_a.608: I say after the example of the Old Doctors of the Church: For Fathers adhering to the PRIOR Exposition Joh. Jonston thus introduces in the Syntagma on the Communion of the Old Church ch. 3 Art. 2 §. 3 pp. 75 and 76: This Eucharistic Body obtains many appellations and epithets among the Fathers: by Augustine it is called Virtue and grace; by Ambrose, Body of the divine Spirit, because it is Spirit; Body of God, which is a spiritual Body; by Jerome spiritual Flesh; intelligible, by Isychius; typic and symbolic Body, by Origen… Bertram calls it a Spiritual Body; a Body which is called God’s mystery, not visible nor palpable; different from the body which is known in Christ’s body already glorified through the resurrection…
pass_a.609: But to the POSTERIOR Exposition those alleged by William Forbes from the Fathers of the Old Church come nearer… To the PRIOR Exposition fewer among the Reformed assent; Among the newer English see Simon Patrick in Mensa mystica… Among Germans, the most Famous man Johann Georg Wachter… Both of these so urge the SPIRITUALITY of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper that they are found expressly to substitute His Spirit in place of Christ’s body. Most follow the POSTERIOR exposition.
pass_a.610: It may seem not alien from our Theological office to have brought into the midst our Marchic Church’s Symbolic Torun Confession on the Lord’s Supper… than which we have seen none concerning the Supper more excellent and fuller: It is clear therefore, say the Torun men, that this Sacrament consists of earthly things, bread and wine, and heavenly, the Lord’s body and blood, which though in a diverse mode are yet both most truly, most really, and most presentingly exhibited to us; namely, the Earthly in a natural, corporal and earthly mode; but the Heavenly in a SPIRITUAL, MYSTICAL AND HEAVENLY MODE, which inscrutable to Reason and sense we hold by Faith alone… Hence also the earthly Thing, Bread and Wine, truly are and are called Christ’s very body and blood, not indeed Substantially or CORPORALLY, but SACRAMENTALLY and MYSTICALLY, or through and on account of the Sacramental union, which consists not in bare Signification, nor only in Sealing, but also in THAT JOINED AND SIMULTANEOUS EXHIBITION AND COMMUNICATION OF THE EARTHLY AND HEAVENLY THING, though diverse in mode.
pass_a.611: This POSTERIOR exposition I also judge the better, adding: The same body of Christ which was crucified for us, and the same blood which was poured out for us, are SPIRITUALLY present in the Supper and SPIRITUALLY received by us — nay even inasmuch as that was crucified and this poured out on the altar of the cross… This comes nearer both to Christ’s Institution words and to the nature of the thing… Whence further the most Illustrious Lutheran Prince Philip Landgrave of Hesse ingeniously collects thus in a Letter to Luther for the Zwinglians…: And since Christ, he writes, because He has a clarified body by which the Belly cannot be fed, can scarcely be eaten otherwise than by Believers and through faith; These things, I say, being so, your sentence seems to me harder and not necessary.
pass_a.612: §. XXIII. Therefore the Reformed’s constant sentence of mind is that Christ’s true and substantial body, which once on earth was emptied, but now in heaven is exalted, is present in the Sacred Supper to modern Communicants always and until Christ is to return to judge the living and the dead, under that quality and in that mode under which quality or in which mode it was present to the first Communicants in the very Sacred use of the Supper: For it is no less obvious to the Reformed Faith that Christ’s crucified body, inasmuch as it is crucified, is present in the Supper (SPIRITUALLY namely) than it remains persuaded to the Lutheran Faith that Christ’s glorified body, and therefore Spiritual inasmuch as such, is yet eaten with the mouth of the body. But to one disputing and arguing either that to be present in the thing itself and to be present Spiritually fight each other, or that a spiritual mode of being present does not fit a body, we cannot but recite what Matthew Wren the Englishman answers most sharply to the Racovian Catechism inferring by a like pact… To the FORMER indeed: Do you say truly, he says, that in the thing itself and spiritually fight? Is the spiritual condition so hostile that it devours the Real?… For the more spiritual a thing is, the more it can be discerned to be…

607: §.XXII: all the Reformed seriously confess the most real presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Supper — in a Spiritual mode.

Yet after the old Doctors they expound that spiritual presence under a light difference in a double way: some put SPIRITUALITY in the body and blood themselves present; others rather in the mode of their presence.
608: PRIOR exposition (Johnston’s Fathers): the Eucharistic Body is called virtue and grace (Augustine); body of the divine Spirit / spiritual body (Ambrose); spiritual flesh (Jerome); typic and symbolic (Origen).
Bertram: a Spiritual Body — God’s mystery, not visible or palpable — different from the already-glorified body known after the resurrection.
609: POSTERIOR exposition sits nearer Forbes’s Fathers. Fewer Reformed hold the prior — among newer English, Patrick’s Mensa mystica; among Germans, Wachter.
Both so urge spirituality that they expressly put Christ’s Spirit in place of His body. Most Reformeds follow the posterior exposition.
610: Torun Confession (Marchic symbolic): the Sacrament is earthly bread and wine plus heavenly body and blood — both most truly and really exhibited, but in diverse modes.

Earthly: natural/corporal; heavenly: SPIRITUAL, MYSTICAL, HEAVENLY mode held by faith alone. Bread and wine are called body and blood sacramentally and mystically — not substantially/corporally — by a joined simultaneous exhibition of earthly and heavenly, not bare signification or sealing only.
611: Strimesius judges the posterior better: the same crucified body and poured blood are SPIRITUALLY present and SPIRITUALLY received — even as crucified and poured on the cross — nearer Institution and the thing’s nature.
Philip of Hesse to Luther for the Zwinglians: a clarified body the belly cannot feed can scarcely be eaten except by believers through faith — so the harder Lutheran sentence seems unnecessary.
612: §.XXIII: Reformed constant mind — the true substantial body once emptied on earth, now exalted in heaven, is present to modern communicants in the same quality/mode as to the first communicants, until the judgment return.

Crucified-as-crucified present SPIRITUALLY is as obvious to them as glorified-body oral eating is to Lutherans. Wren vs Racovian: ‘really’ and ‘spiritually’ do not fight — the more spiritual, the more a thing is. Stop mid-XXIII (Wren’s second reply remains).
